DMS_AirportAssault.questDescriptionRules.li:
questDescription->Intercepted telemetry points to a [siteFactionName] drone airfield. The field is still active: a garrison of (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat) patrols the tower and the aprons, and the tower's decoy radio is still tuned to the command band of the cluster weaver.

That radio is the prize. Clear the field and it can be used to call the weaver down onto the airfield, on ground of your choosing, far from your colony. Whatever the mothership drops when it falls is yours to strip.

Beneath the aprons there is also a freight elevator into a buried storage vault. Its blast doors answer to two security consoles in the tower; hack both to open the shaft.

The telemetry fix holds for [siteTimeout]. After that the field goes dark and its position is lost.

The installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.

Caution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown, and the weaver will not wait for you to finish with them.

DMS_LegacyInstallationAssault.questDescr.li:
questDescription(installation==DMS_VaultStationSite)->A supply manifest recovered from remnant traffic lists a [siteFactionName] storage vault, and the surface station that sits on top of it. The station is still manned by (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat), and heavy units are among them.

The freight elevator into the vault is locked under an armored cover plate. The station's security console is the only thing that can raise it; hack it and the shaft opens. The car still has power, so what is below was never collected.

The manifest's location fix expires in [siteTimeout]. After that the station will relocate and its position will be lost.

The installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.

Caution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown. Get the shaft open, then decide whether to hold the surface or go down.

questDescription(installation==DMS_RepairStationSite)->A maintenance request on the remnant network leads to a [siteFactionName] field repair depot. The depot is guarded by (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat): engineers, riflemen and a drone screen.

Two units are still clamped in the depot's cradles, in hibernation, behind a sealed maintenance door. They were never re-authenticated after servicing, so a mechanitor with spare bandwidth can hack one and take it. The depot's security console releases the door. There is also a mobile crew lifter on the pad and a stock of tungsteel in the stores.

The request's location fix expires in [siteTimeout]. After that the depot will relocate and its position will be lost.

The installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.

Caution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown.

questDescription(installation==DMS_OperationBaseSite)->Remnant traffic has given away a [siteFactionName] forward operating base. It is held by (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat): line infantry behind the wire, with heavy support and night-capable units in reserve.

The base is a supply hub. Crates of rations, small arms, spare parts and prosthetics sit in the open, and a freight elevator at the back of the compound leads down into a buried store. The blast doors in front of it answer to two security consoles; hack both to open the way, then hack the lift itself.

The position fix holds for [siteTimeout]. After that the base will strike camp and its position will be lost.

The installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.

Caution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown.

questDescription(installation==DMS_SiteStationSite)->A pre-war station, half of it collapsed, has been located nearby. A [siteFactionName] detachment has dug into the ruins: (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat), shield-bearers and infantry with drone and lifter support, spread across the station's halls.

The station was abandoned in a hurry. Ancient supply crates, industrial shelving and the wrecks of the old security systems are still scattered through it, along with a working pod launcher pair. Everything the detachment has not already stripped is yours.

The detachment is expected to move on in [siteTimeout]. After that the station will be picked clean and no longer worth the trip.

The installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.

One of the station's freight elevators still runs down to a data archive the fleet buried beneath it. A facility server core sits in the sealed server hall at the bottom; it can be hacked several times, and every attempt will bring the archive's defences up from below. The corridors are fitted with gas vents, and a lockdown controller will seal the lift a minute after the alert level maxes out.

Caution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown, and the station is large enough to get lost in.

questDescription(installation==DMS_LaunchSiteSite)->An old missile launch complex has turned up on the scanners. The launchers were destroyed long ago and the compound is falling apart, but a [siteFactionName] patrol of (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat) still sweeps the wreckage.

Nobody ever salvaged the place. Wrecked automatroids, a logistics container, sensor and radar mounts and the remains of the launch crews' equipment are all still where they fell.

The patrol's schedule puts it there for another [siteTimeout]. After that it moves on and the site's position is lost.

The installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.

Caution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, the patrol's monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown.
